items.title: Physician: The outdated mindset that gets in the way of our healing
items.description:
Physician Giulia Enders spent years studying the gut before realizing no organ works alone. Here, she walks through 5 body parts — the lung, the immune system, the skin, the muscles, and the brain — and what each one reveals about how we work, heal, and recover. 
 This video  Physician: The outdated mindset that gets in the way of our healing  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: The psychology of revenge, in 19 minutes
items.description:
Psychologist Paul Bloom explains why morality, the thing that makes cooperation and trust possible, is also what drives cruelty, cycles of revenge, and wars where both sides believe they’re the moral ones. 
 This video  The psychology of revenge, in 19 minutes  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: How Ice-T evolved out of ‘survival mode’
items.description:
From writing ‘Cop Killer’ to playing a cop on  SVU , ICE-T is no stranger to personal evolution. After losing both parents by seventh grade, he was sent to Los Angeles, where he learned to survive without a family. Here, he hustled for money and respect until rap gave him another route.

items.title: The value of time off isn’t better productivity — it’s your humanity
items.description:
As humans, we instinctively understand that time has profound worth, regardless of any workplace benefits. This is what sabbatical alumni mean when they ascribe a feeling of humanity to their time off. items.title: The goal-setting mistake you don’t know you’re making
items.description:
I have struggled to set goals for most of my life. I’ve wondered for a while what they actually do for me. When I was younger, my dad had us write down big, ambitious, long-term goals. I still have some of those handwritten notes.

items.title: Ask Ethan: Should we stop worrying about vacuum decay?
items.description: When we gaze out into the abyss of space, it seems like the most peaceful, serene of sights. items.title: 2026’s Perseids, lousy this July, will peak at the perfect time
items.description: During most times of the year, when you look up at a dark, clear night sky, the stars, planets, and perhaps the Moon shine brightly, along with, if you’re lucky, a view of the plane of the Milky Way. As far as objects moving through the sky go, you’re usually far more likely to see things with artificial lights, like airplanes or satellites, than you are meteors.
